scenario.title: Stack overflow without the MPU - watermark hits 100 percent, then corruption
scenario.description: The same overflowing task C as P07, but the kernel never enables the MPU. C's stack grows past its base, through the unused guard bytes and into the neighbouring task stacks and globals. The watermark of C reaches 100 percent before anything goes wrong; then other tasks resume with corrupted frames, and eventually an exception return pops a garbage frame (INVPC UsageFault) or a push reaches unmapped memory (BusFault). Compare the fault list and the task states with P07.

expected.summary: No MemManage; instead a late BusFault/UsageFault chain, more than one task dead, C's watermark 100 percent and corrupted globals.

scenario.what_to_look_for: The mpu event says "MPU left disabled". After the marker "deep recursion begins" there is a long gap with no fault: C's watermark climbs to 100 percent (visible in the watermarks attached to context_switch events) and C keeps writing below its stack base. Later faults appear in the wrong places: a BusFault from C when the stack finally reaches the bottom of SRAM, then UsageFault INVPC events from tasks A and B whose saved frames were overwritten (xPSR with a nonsense exception number, PC near 0). The globals a_iters and corruptions hold garbage like 0xDEAD-derived values. Several tasks end DEAD, versus exactly one in P07.
likely_root_causes: A task overflowed its stack and the system has no MPU guard, so the damage lands in whatever was linked below: another task's stack, the TCB array or globals.
The symptom (a fault in task A) is far from the cause (task C), which is the signature of memory corruption.
how_to_debug: Add stack watermarks: fill each stack with 0xA5A5A5A5 at creation and report the deepest overwritten word; a task at 100 percent is the culprit even if another task crashed.
Place a canary word below each stack and check it at every tick; the first broken canary names the overflowing task.
Enable the MPU with a guard region per task (P07) so the first bad write faults immediately with the address in MMFAR.
In the fault handler, print the stacked frame: a PC that is not inside any function and an xPSR with a wrong exception number means the frame itself was overwritten.
scenario.what_this_means: Memory corruption is not detected where it happens but where its victim runs. The watermark is the early-warning instrument: it climbs before the crash. The MPU is the containment instrument: it converts the first bad write into a precise fault. P07 and P09 are the same bug with and without that containment, which is why the course asks for both.
scenario.hidden_symptom: Random tasks crash with UsageFault or BusFault at nonsense addresses; which one crashes changes with timing.

events.reason: scenario P09: Stack overflow without the MPU - watermark hits 100 percent, then corruption

faults: task_overflows_stack: Task C recurses without bound and runs off the bottom of its stack.
no_mpu: The kernel never enables the MPU: a stack overflow silently corrupts the neighbour.
